subject: Next steps: strawman economics & token thresholds for new feature
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@medilabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + strawman economics (asks)

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a small strawman so we can align before the pricing/finance call: 

1) What we heard from product: launch will target an initial cohort of ~20k MAU (feature gate), ramping to ~200k MAU over 12 months if engagement signals validate.
2) Expected usage (your input requested): average calls per MAU/day and expected avg tokens per call (prompt + completion).
3) Budget guidance you gave on the call: high-level range ~$20k–$40k/month initial (we'll need to confirm).

Strawman economics (for discussion):
- Token range (initial): ~1.8M tokens/day (20k MAU * 0.18 calls/MAU/day * 500 tokens avg) => ~54M tokens/month.
- Target unit: $/1M tokens target for customer economics that you mentioned: $80–$150 per 1M tokens.
- Example per-feature unit: if we price the feature as an add-on at $3.50/MAU/month, with your 20k MAU that’s $70k/month gross. With inference cost at $120/1M tokens and the strawman token burn above, margin math gets tight — we should model both per-MAU and per-token pricing.

Can you confirm (reply inline) the two items below so we can finalize an initial pricing strawman for finance: 
- Confirm initial MAU target and expected ramp timeline (20k initial -> ? by month 6/12)
- Confirm average tokens per call (ballpark prompt+response length) and expected calls per MAU/day

I attached a simple workbook (redwood-strawman-econ-v1.xlsx) with cells you can update. Once we have those figures we’ll send a short note with two recommended commercial structures (per-feature add-on vs. token-based pilot) and estimated CAC payback at 6/9/12 month targets.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-strawman-econ-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Emma Carter <emma@medilabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + strawman economics (asks)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. Quick answers below (happy to follow up with a short spreadsheet if it helps):

- MAU and ramp: initial gated launch 20k MAU (week 0), expected ramp to ~80k MAU by month 6 and ~200k MAU by month 12 if the beta engagement holds.
- Calls per MAU/day: we expect ~0.18–0.22 calls/MAU/day initially (conservative).
- Average tokens per call: our UX team believes typical prompt + answer will be ~500 tokens; with some longer flows (1k tokens) but those are ~10% of calls.
- Initial budget: leadership allocated roughly $25k–$35k/mo for the pilot month(s); can expand if we see clear conversion.

Additional notes: MediLabs’ product team wants CAC payback under 9 months for add-on monetization (rule of thumb). Procurement will need an SOC2 summary and a short pilot SOW for finance.

If you can send the two commercial structures with example math (we prefer a short one-pager), I’ll route to finance and PM for quick review.

Best,
Emma Carter
Head of Product | MediLabs
[Attachment: MediLabs-feature-spec.pdf (doc)]
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + strawman economics (asks) — MediLabs details & ask list

Ben / Aditya — forwarding Emma’s reply. Key inputs are below; I sketched a quick internal strawman and asks for modeling. Can one of you take the workbook and return a short two-option commercial recommendation by EOD tomorrow?

Inputs from prospect (copied):
- Initial MAU: 20k -> 80k @6mo -> 200k @12mo
- Calls/MAU/day: 0.18–0.22
- Avg tokens/call: ~500 (10% at 1k)
- Budget: $25k–$35k/mo initial
- CAC payback target: <9 months

My quick calculations (rough):
- Initial tokens/day = 20,000 * 0.18 * 500 = 1,800,000 tokens/day (~54M tokens/mo)
- If we assume Redwood cost = $120 / 1M tokens (current median for similar profiles), monthly inference cost = 54 * $120 = $6,480/month.
- If the feature drives $3.50/MAU/month (per-feature add-on example), revenue at 20k MAU = $70k/month gross. That leaves healthy room for CAC and other costs, but only if actual usage and model selection keep inference unit cost near our assumed $120/1M tokens.

Proposed two commercial structures to model (please return numbers for each at MAU = 20k / 80k / 200k):
A) Per-feature add-on: flat $X / MAU / month + pilot credits (e.g., 1M tokens free)
B) Token-based pilot: $Y per 1M tokens with step-down tiers at volume thresholds + committed monthly minimum

Please include:
- Estimated monthly inference cost (assuming current runtime profiles and possible 15% cost reduction with batching/quantization)
- Example CAC payback in months, assuming 20% conversion to paid feature at launch and a blended LTV take rate (use conservative churn 3%/mo)
- Sensitivity: $/1M tokens at $100, $120, $150 buckets and headroom to margin targets (30–50% gross margin on the feature).

I’m happy to take the final deck to Emma and finance; want to propose a short commercial call end of next week (Thu 7/16) to review.

Thanks — Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + strawman economics (asks) — MediLabs details & ask list

Thanks Lauren — good summary. Quick ops points from SE side and asks for the pricing model: 

- Cost assumptions: we can model three kernel/model families: small/cheap (quantized) at ~$80/1M tokens, medium at ~$120/1M, and high-quality large at ~$220/1M. With batching + KV caching we historically see 10–25% effective unit cost reduction depending on request distribution; I included both conservative (10%) and optimistic (25%) scenarios in the workbook.
- Pilot suggestion: offer 1 month free up to 10M tokens + a short-term commitment at the $120/1M tier; if volume > 50M/mo shift to $100/1M with billing true-up. This preserves margin while showing runway.
- Procurement asks: Emma — we can attach SOC2 summary and a stub SOW. Who should I coordinate with on the procurement side (procurement@medilabs.com or finance@medilabs.com)? Also confirm whether SSO + SCIM required for pilot.

I’ll take Lauren’s proposed two structures and plug real cost bands (80/120/220) and the batching deltas across the three MAU scenarios. Expect a return workbook by tomorrow EOD with pivot tables for CAC payback at 20% conversion / conservative churn.

Ben
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
